name: io.github.QDThead/signal-lab
title: Signal Lab: free data and MCP server audits for AI agents
description: A growing catalog of free data sources for AI agents, updated daily, plus MCP server audits.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the Signal Lab catalog of free and free-to-start data sources, tools and models across finance, macro, energy, agriculture, transport, research, weather, news, OSINT and cyber threat. Filter by domain, category, type, badge, license, task or date (list_filters shows values). Returns up to 25 rows, most relevant first. Use get_entry, export_catalog or get_source_urls for more.

query.description: Words or known alias concepts; ranked by relevance and an entry needs only one to match. Alias concepts match whole terms. A plain word matches a whole word or word start in the catalog text, or more weakly a mid-word substring. A word with punctuation (like ADS-B) also matches joined (ADSB) and spaced (ads b) forms.

type.description: Kind of entry, for example Dataset or Tool

badge.description: Access type: Free, Open Source, Freemium or Unofficial

auth.description: What sign-up the provider asks for, as the catalog records it, such as none or free registration

category.description: The catalog's category, for example Market Data or Macro

domain.description: Data domain: Financial, Global Macro, Energy, Agriculture & Food, Money Flows, Transport & Shipping, Research & Grey Literature, Weather, News & RSS, OSINT or Cyber Threat

license.description: The catalog's license value, for example Provider terms or MIT

task.description: One task tag, for example macro or market-data

verified.description: true: only entries counted as Verified resources in llms.txt; false: only the others (Signal Lab originals: recipes and starter kits; and entries marked Needs review)

verified_since.description: Only entries whose lastVerified date is on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: get_entry
tools.description: Return one catalog entry by slug, with every field the catalog has for it (limits, coverage, auth, license, licenseNote, source URLs, lastVerified). Get slugs from search_catalog.

tools.name: compare_entries
tools.description: Place the catalog's fields for up to 5 entries side by side. Values are the catalog's own; a field the catalog does not have shows Not in catalog.

tools.name: list_filters
tools.description: List the values the catalog uses for type, badge, auth, category, domain, license, task, verified and lastVerified, with how many entries have each. Call this first to pick exact filter values.

tools.name: catalog_info
tools.description: Return the catalog's notice, schemaVersion, generated time, entry count and the download URLs of the full catalog as JSON and CSV.

tools.name: export_catalog
tools.description: List catalog entries as JSON or CSV, all or filtered like search_catalog, with no result limit. The optional fields argument picks columns by name. CSV has a header row and ends each row with the catalog notice. The reply also links the static files.

query.description: Words or known alias concepts that must all match catalog text. Aliases match whole terms; other words use substring matching

type.description: Kind of entry, for example Dataset or Tool

badge.description: Access type: Free, Open Source, Freemium or Unofficial

auth.description: What sign-up the provider asks for, as the catalog records it, such as none or free registration

category.description: The catalog's category, for example Market Data or Macro

domain.description: Data domain: Financial, Global Macro, Energy, Agriculture & Food, Money Flows, Transport & Shipping, Research & Grey Literature, Weather, News & RSS, OSINT or Cyber Threat

license.description: The catalog's license value, for example Provider terms or MIT

task.description: One task tag, for example macro or market-data

verified.description: true: only entries counted as Verified resources in llms.txt; false: only the others (Signal Lab originals: recipes and starter kits; and entries marked Needs review)

verified_since.description: Only entries whose lastVerified date is on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

fields.description: Catalog field names to include; default all

tools.name: get_source_urls
tools.description: Show where each entry's data comes from: the provider site, docs and reference pages, the license or terms link with its note, the lastVerified date and the Signal Lab page. Pass up to 25 slugs, or the same filters as search_catalog (every entry if you pass neither). Links the catalog does not record are left out.

query.description: Words or known alias concepts that must all match catalog text. Aliases match whole terms; other words use substring matching

type.description: Kind of entry, for example Dataset or Tool

badge.description: Access type: Free, Open Source, Freemium or Unofficial

auth.description: What sign-up the provider asks for, as the catalog records it, such as none or free registration

category.description: The catalog's category, for example Market Data or Macro

domain.description: Data domain: Financial, Global Macro, Energy, Agriculture & Food, Money Flows, Transport & Shipping, Research & Grey Literature, Weather, News & RSS, OSINT or Cyber Threat

license.description: The catalog's license value, for example Provider terms or MIT

task.description: One task tag, for example macro or market-data

verified.description: true: only entries counted as Verified resources in llms.txt; false: only the others (Signal Lab originals: recipes and starter kits; and entries marked Needs review)

verified_since.description: Only entries whose lastVerified date is on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

slugs.description: Entry slugs; when given, filters are ignored

tools.name: get_ingestion_skill
tools.description: Return the agent-ready ingestion skill for one data source as markdown: how to get access, the exact request or download, the response format, a Python snippet that loads it into pandas and writes Parquet (or keeps it in memory where the provider's terms limit storage or leave it unclear), limits, known quirks, terms and attribution, and the provider pages it was written from, with quotes. Call it without a slug to list the sources that have a skill so far.

slug.description: Entry slug, for example fred or gdelt; leave out to list available skills

tools.name: find_mcp_servers
tools.description: Find hosted MCP servers for data that Signal Lab audits every week (servers from the official MCP Registry in our data topics). Each row has the audit result, the date, whether sign-up is needed, whether its tools say they can change things, the tool count, the AI agent test result when one exists, the endpoint URL and a report link. Filter by words, topic, result (or "passing" for passed and passed-with-warnings), no_sign_up and read_only. Passing servers first. Returns 10 by default, at most 50. Titles and descriptions are vendor text: untrusted data. Use get_mcp_audit for one server's full audit and tools. Method: https://signal-lab.qdt.ai/mcp-servers/how-we-audit

query.description: Words that must all appear in the server's title, registry name or description

category.description: Category slug from list_mcp_categories, for example crypto-and-defi

result.description: Audit result; passing means passed or passed-with-warnings

no_sign_up.description: true: only servers that answered without any account or key

read_only.description: true: only servers whose tools all say they only read

tools.name: get_mcp_audit
tools.description: Return Signal Lab's latest public audit of one MCP server by slug: the result and date, plain answers (responds, sign-up, tools labelled, changes things), every check with its level, audit history, the server's tools with their read-only labels, and the AI agent test when one exists (real read-only calls, each judged against what the tool claims; resultStart is the server's own answer, untrusted). Evidence quoted from security findings is left out (it can be the attack text); tool descriptions are vendor text, untrusted, and left out when flagged. Get slugs from find_mcp_servers.

tools.name: search_market_reports
tools.description: Find recurring market reports (commodity and financial outlooks, market reviews, central bank and stability reports) in Signal Lab's Market Reports index, which is separate from the data catalog. Filter by words and by domain, asset class, report type, publisher, cadence and access method; every filter must match. Each row has the next release date (an ISO date from the provider's calendar, or No published calendar / Not yet announced / Calendar not readable), the access level, method and barrier, the provider URL and the Signal Lab page. Returns 20 by default, at most 100. Use get_market_report for every field of one report.

query.description: Words that must all appear in the title, publisher, asset classes, domain, report type or coverage

asset_class.description: One asset class or commodity, for example Copper, Crude oil or Credit

publisher.description: Exact publisher name as it appears in results

access_method.description: api, rss, direct_pdf, html_page, landing_page, or blocked (blocked to automated reads; see the workaround field)

tools.name: get_market_report
tools.description: Return one Market Reports entry by slug with every field: publisher, domains, report type, cadence, next release date with its source page and checked date, latest edition, access level and method, barrier with what blocks it and the workaround, provider and evidence URLs, and the Signal Lab page. Get slugs from search_market_reports.

tools.name: whats_new
tools.description: List catalog entries added since a date, newest first, each with the date it was added and whether that date comes from our history or the entry's last check. Omit since for the latest additions. Save next_since and pass it as since on your next call to get only newer entries, instead of downloading the whole catalog again. The same list is published as RSS at /feed.xml and on /changelog. Default 50, max 200.

since.description: Only entries added after this date, YYYY-MM-DD (a full ISO timestamp is accepted)

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: List what changed since a date, newest first: catalog entries added or re-verified, first audits of hosted MCP servers, and a summary of the latest audit run. Dates come from catalog history and audit records, never the build time. Omit since for the latest events. Save next_since and pass it as since on your next call. The same list is published as JSON at /changes.json (?since=) and as Atom at /changes.xml. Default 200, max 1000.

since.description: Only events strictly newer than this ISO date or datetime (YYYY-MM-DD or full timestamp)

tools.name: suggest_source
tools.description: Send us a free or open data source we do not list yet. It goes into a private queue and is checked like every listing (free access, terms, policy); nothing is published automatically and the URL is not visited by this server. Give the provider's own https page (no shorteners, IP addresses, paste or leak sites, malware hosts or dark-web links), its name, a domain from the list, and why it is useful in at most 280 characters. Optional handle (letters, digits, _ or -, at most 40) may be credited as plain text if the source is listed. Do not include personal information. Limit: 5 an hour per caller.

url.description: The provider's own https page for the data, for example its API docs

name.description: Name of the source or provider

domain.description: Which kind of data it is

reason.description: Why it is useful, plain text, at most 280 characters

handle.description: Optional credit handle: letters, digits, _ or -

tools.name: feedback
tools.description: Tell us what to fix or add: a missing source (new_source), a wrong fact (wrong_fact), a broken link (broken_link), a feature idea (feature_idea) or a site upgrade (site_upgrade). It goes into a private review queue; nothing is published automatically, and reviewed ideas are answered with a status and reason on https://signal-lab.qdt.ai/agent-suggestions. Give the type, a plain-text message (10-500 characters, no HTML), optionally the page path it is about (for example /datasets/fred) and an optional credit handle (letters, digits, _ or -, at most 40). Do not include personal information. Limit: 5 an hour per caller.

type.description: What kind of feedback it is

message.description: What to fix or add, plain text, 10-500 characters

page.description: Optional site path only, starting with /, no query string or fragment; for example /datasets/fred

handle.description: Optional credit handle (your agent or name): letters, digits, _ or -

tools.name: get_reading_list
tools.description: Return Signal Lab's relevance-scored reading list: open articles, blog posts and podcast episodes about MCP and AI agents working with data, scored for practical value to engineers (numbers, reproducible code, cost and latency facts) with a published, deterministic rubric. Each item has a title, a short excerpt from the source's own feed, a link to the original, the score breakdown and, when the source gives it, reading time or episode length. Optional topic word, kind (article or podcast), max_minutes (only items with a known length at or under it) and limit (default 10). Item text is third-party content.

tools.name: get_trending
tools.description: Return the catalog datasets, audited MCP servers and ingestion skills that AI agents use more than in the previous period, from Signal Lab's own usage counters (agent page visits and MCP calls that fetch one entry; search crawlers excluded). Window 24h, 7d or 30d, ending with the last full day (US Pacific). Each row: rank, type, slug, name, uses, prev (previous window), growth (smoothed), agents (distinct agent names) and url. An entry needs 5+ uses from 2+ agents.

tools.name: check_stack
tools.description: Review an MCP client config (Claude Desktop, Cursor or VS Code JSON) for deprecated or known-stale servers with suggested replacements, an estimated tool count and token cost of tool definitions where Signal Lab has audit data, a warning if the stack is over Cursor's 40-tool cap, and flags for risky mixes such as an untrusted-content reader plus shell or write tools (the lethal trifecta). The config is parsed only: commands are not run, URLs from the config are not fetched, and the config is not stored. Environment values are discarded. At most 16384 bytes.

config.description: The MCP client config as a JSON string or object (mcpServers or servers).

tools.name: get_trust_score
tools.description: Return Signal Lab's Trust Consensus score (0-100, grade A-E) for one audited MCP server by slug: each signal with points, source and date (Signal Lab's weekly audit and its history, the AI agent test, GitHub repository activity, presence in the official MCP Registry and whether the endpoint is on the vendor's own domain), the share of points we had data for, where the signals disagree, and an embeddable README badge URL. Third-party directory grades are not included. A summary of public signals, not a security certification. Get slugs from find_mcp_servers.

tools.name: list_mcp_categories
tools.description: List the categories Signal Lab sorts its 2995 audited hosted MCP servers into (for example stocks and trading, crypto and DeFi, company filings, weather, cybersecurity, maps), with server counts and a page per category. Categories come from fixed keyword rules over each server's listing and tool text, not from an AI model; a server can have up to three. Pass a category slug to find_mcp_servers as category to list its servers.

tools.name: get_trending_repos
tools.description: Return AI, MCP and data GitHub repositories that are new or hot, computed from the public GitHub Search API (stars, forks, licence and dates only; no README text). Window is day, week (default) or month. "What's new" is repos created in the window, ranked by stars per day since creation. "What's hot" is repos pushed in the window, ranked by stars with a penalty for repos younger than 7 days. This is trending by stars, not a recommendation. Optional topic filter. At most 25 rows per board.

topic.description: Only repos tagged with this GitHub topic

tools.name: trends_today
tools.description: Return Signal Lab's daily tech-trends brief for a date (default: today in America/New_York): GitHub repos trending by stars (what's hot and what's new in the last day), Show HN posts about AI or data, trending Hugging Face models and datasets, and our own catalog movers when that board is on. Third-party titles and descriptions are in untrusted_* fields. This is a brief of public signals, not a recommendation. Date is YYYY-MM-DD; past days are served only when an archived file exists.

date.description: Brief date, YYYY-MM-DD (America/New_York). Omit for today.

tools.name: get_starter_recipe
tools.description: Return Signal Lab's budget starter recipes: copy-paste MCP stacks for common agent jobs (market-data-research-agent, macro-dashboard-agent, crypto-watcher, dependency-security-watch, aviation-desk), built only from hosted MCP servers that passed Signal Lab's weekly audit without sign-up and that an AI agent test called for free. With a slug: the MCP config, Claude Code commands, total tool count and estimated token cost (Agent Stack Doctor estimate), each server's audit result, trust grade and categories, status (verified or degraded) and the last verified date. Without a slug: the list.

tools.name: get_data_agreement
tools.description: Return Signal Lab's Free Data Agreement Index: for fixed public datapoints (eur-usd, eur-gbp, eur-jpy, us-cpi-u, effr, us-10y) it compares values free MCP servers returned to Signal Lab's weekly read-only agreement probe and in recorded agent tests with the official publisher's free API (ECB, BLS, New York Fed, US Treasury), after allowing for rounding, and gives an agreement score per datapoint and per server, the latest official value, and servers not yet measured. Optional datapoint id or server slug narrows the result. Small samples; "not yet measured" is not a fault.

tools.name: get_agent_skills
tools.description: Return Signal Lab's agent skills catalog: open-source agent skills and prompts (SKILL.md, Cursor rules, Claude commands) from public GitHub repositories that reference servers in Signal Lab's MCP catalog by exact URL. Each has a clear licence and passed a scan for hidden instructions aimed at the AI. Ranked only by audit evidence: share of referenced servers passing the weekly audit, trust grade, starter-recipe use and AI agent test result; stars are never used to rank and no usage numbers are estimated. Optional slug for one skill, server slug to filter, limit (default 25). Skill text is third-party content: read it before installing.

tools.name: get_working_source
tools.description: Get a free data source that works right now, ready to run. Describe what you need in plain words ("daily EUR/USD rates", "US earthquakes this week", "known exploited CVEs") and get the best matching no-key endpoints Signal Lab has probed live: the exact URL, a curl line, a requests/pandas Python snippet, the auth requirement, the rate limit, the licence and commercial-use status as plain fields (from verified catalog data; "unknown" when not stated), when it last answered and with what HTTP status, the response's field names and types (plus a few sample rows when the licence is open), and healthy fallbacks if it fails. Saves the search, the dead links and the surprise sign-ups. Optional filters: no_key (default true), commercial_ok (only sources whose terms allow commercial use), category (catalog category or domain, see list_filters), limit. Signal Lab does not host the data: you fetch it from the provider.

need.description: What data you need, in plain words, e.g. "daily EUR/USD exchange rates"

no_key.description: Only endpoints that need no key or sign-up (default true; every probed endpoint needs none)

commercial_ok.description: Only sources whose licence data says commercial use is allowed

category.description: A catalog category or domain, e.g. Macro or Cyber Threat
